svg.title: P016 · December 2025 orders with customer names
svg.desc: One row per December order with a matching customer. Customer 1 matches two orders, 10 and 11. The inner join keeps both matched pairs at this stage. Order 10 qualifies on December 1. Order 11 is dated January 1 of the following year and drops out. The remaining order displays Anu Sen, Delhi and 100. The query sorts by order date and ID. First · FROM Customers. The saved query begins with known customers because they supply the name and city for the call sheet. Second · INNER JOIN Orders. Match the two CustomerID columns. Only an order with a known customer belongs on the call sheet. Either table can come first in this inner join and produce the same pairs.
svg.text: One row per December order with a matching customer.
Both orders belong to Anu. Which operation removes the January order?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Double underlines mark the matching keys. Dots inside quotes show
padding. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
Which pairs satisfy the customer lookup?

g.text: The saved query begins with known customers because they supply the name and city for the call sheet.
Match the two CustomerID columns. Only an order with a known customer belongs on the call sheet. Either table can
come first in this inner join and produce the same pairs.

svg.text: Customer 1 matches two orders, 10 and 11. The inner join keeps both matched pairs at this stage.
Customers INNER JOIN Orders ON Customers.CustomerID = Orders.CustomerID
Which matched orders fall in December 2025?
Order 10 qualifies on December 1. Order 11 is dated January 1 of the following year and drops out.
What belongs on the call sheet?
The remaining order displays Anu Sen, Delhi and 100. The query sorts by order date and ID.
